changes.old: This article addresses adaptive event-triggered control for interval type-2 (IT-2) fuzzy cyber-physical systems (CPSs) affected by stochastic deception attacks and Markov-type actuator failures. Since nonlinear CPSs face cyber-layer attacks as well as physical-layer component failures, while their communication resources are often limited, an adaptive event-triggered mechanism (AETM) is employed to reduce redundant network transmissions through dynamic adjustment of the triggering threshold based on real-time state-error information. Specifically, stochastic deception attacks are characterized by a Bernoulli process, and actuator failures are modeled by Markov switching fault matrices. Accordingly, a unified closed-loop model is established. Then, a looped functional dependent on fuzzy membership functions (FMFs) is constructed to exploit membership-function information and sampled-data dynamics. Based on this functional, stability criteria are obtained to guarantee asymptotic stability of the closed-loop system while achieving a prescribed $\mathrm{H}_\infty$ disturbance attenuation level. Moreover, joint design of the controller gains and adaptive triggering parameters is formulated through tractable linear matrix inequalities (LMIs). Validation is finally carried out with an engineering-motivated permanent magnet synchronous motor example and a numerical IT-2 fuzzy system to demonstrate the effectiveness and feasibility of the developed method.
changes.new: This article addresses adaptive event-triggered control for interval type-2 (IT-2) fuzzy cyber-physical systems (CPSs) subject to stochastic deception attacks and Markov-type actuator failures. An adaptive event-triggered mechanism (AETM) adjusts the transmission threshold using state-error information to reduce redundant communication. Deception attacks are described by a Bernoulli process, and actuator failures are represented by Markov switching fault matrices. These components are incorporated into a unified closed-loop model. The signs of the membership-function derivatives define operational regions for a region-dependent fuzzy controller. Within this framework, the controller gains and event-triggering weight matrices are jointly designed. A two-sided looped functional dependent on fuzzy membership functions (FMFs) incorporates membership information and sampled-data dynamics. Sufficient conditions for asymptotic stability with a prescribed $\mathrm{H}_\infty$ disturbance attenuation level are formulated as linear matrix inequalities (LMIs). A permanent magnet synchronous motor example and a numerical IT-2 fuzzy example illustrate the control responses and the reduction in data transmissions.

Recent work has further developed event-triggered security control for IT-2 fuzzy systems. Liu et al.\ \cite{liuTorusEventBased2025} combined a two-threshold torus-event-triggering protocol with sliding-mode control for discrete-time IT-2 fuzzy systems under deception attacks. Chandrasekar et al.\ \cite{chandrasekarAdaptiveEvent2026} investigated adaptive event-triggered asynchronous control of uncertain IT-2 fuzzy Markov jump systems, using a hidden Markov model to describe the mismatch between plant and controller modes. These studies provide relevant developments in communication scheduling and attack-resilient fuzzy control. The present study focuses on continuous-time IT-2 fuzzy CPSs with Bernoulli deception attacks and Markov-type actuator failures, and organizes the controller and triggering design around the signs of the membership-function derivatives.

changes.old: This section presents the main results. On the basis of the established system model, an appropriate Lyapunov functional is constructed to obtain sufficient criteria guaranteeing the asymptotic stability and prescribed $\mathrm{H}_\infty$ performance of the closed-loop system.
changes.new: This section develops the analysis and synthesis conditions in three stages. Theorem~\ref{thm1} gives sufficient stability and $\mathrm{H}_\infty$ performance conditions for the closed-loop model. Theorem~\ref{thm2} introduces transformed decision variables to express the joint design of the controller gains and event-triggering weight matrix. Theorem~\ref{thm3} then bounds the actuator-failure uncertainty and yields deterministic LMIs for numerical synthesis. This sequence connects the performance analysis to the gain and triggering-matrix calculations used in the examples.

changes.old: This section considers an engineering-motivated example and a numerical simulation study to assess the effectiveness and applicability of the developed control scheme.
changes.new: Two examples illustrate complementary aspects of the proposed scheme. Example~\ref{exm1} uses a permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) model to provide an engineering context and reports transmission counts for several values of $\sigma$. Example~\ref{exm2} considers a different IT-2 fuzzy model under a fixed parameter setting. In both examples, the state responses, control inputs, actuator-failure modes, adaptive thresholds, and transmission intervals illustrate the closed-loop behavior and communication activity.

changes.old: This study has addressed adaptive event-triggered $\mathrm{H}_{\infty}$ control of IT-2 fuzzy CPSs affected simultaneously by stochastic deception attacks and Markov-type actuator failures. An AETM has been employed to limit unnecessary data transmissions by updating the triggering threshold online using real-time state-error information. In addition, a region-dependent piecewise fuzzy control strategy has been developed by incorporating derivative information from the membership functions. Based on an FMF-dependent and time-dependent looped functional, stability criteria have been obtained to guarantee closed-loop asymptotic stability while achieving a prescribed $\mathrm{H}_{\infty}$ disturbance attenuation level. The controller gains and adaptive event-triggering weight matrices have been jointly determined through tractable LMIs, while a bounding technique has been employed to address the norm-bounded uncertainty induced by Markov-type actuator failures.
changes.new: This study has considered adaptive event-triggered $\mathrm{H}_{\infty}$ control of IT-2 fuzzy CPSs subject to stochastic deception attacks and Markov-type actuator failures. The AETM updates its threshold using state-error information to reduce redundant transmissions. Membership-function derivative information defines operational regions for the fuzzy control design. An FMF-dependent looped functional is used to formulate sufficient stability and performance conditions. The controller gains and event-triggering weight matrices are jointly determined through LMIs, with a bounding technique used to handle actuator-failure uncertainty.
